name: Ceftaroline
executiveSummary: Anti-MRSA cephalosporin. Adult **600 mg IV every 12 h** (skin/CAP). Pediatrics by age/weight: **6–12 mg/kg every 8 h** or **600 mg every 12 h** if ≥12 years and ≥33 kg. Restricted use.
indications:
## Indications

- Complicated skin and soft-tissue infections (including MRSA).
- Community-acquired pneumonia.
- MRSA bacteremia / respiratory focus: ID only (intensified institutional regimens).

## Precautions

- Strict renal adjustment. Positive Coombs test common.
- Infusion usually **60–120 min** per local label/protocol.

> Not a carbapenem; does not replace anti-Pseudomonas spectrum.

adulto.dose: Skin / CAP: **600 mg IV every 12 h**. Renal: CrCl 30–50 → **400 mg q12h**; 15–30 → **300 mg q12h**; ESRD/HD → **200 mg q12h** (post-HD if on dialysis).
adulto.administration: Reconstitute 20 mL SW; dilute in 250 mL NS/D5W (≈2.4 mg/mL); infuse **60 min** (some protocols 120 min).
adulto.notes: Specialist indication for persistent MRSA bacteremia.

pediatrico.dose: 0–2 months: **6 mg/kg every 8 h**. >2 months–<2 years: **8 mg/kg every 8 h**. 2–<12 years: **12 mg/kg every 8 h** (max **400 mg**/dose). 12–<18 years <33 kg: **12 mg/kg every 8 h** (max **400 mg**). 12–<18 years ≥33 kg and adults: **600 mg every 12 h**.
pediatrico.notes: Pediatric renal adjustment by CrCl and weight (Garrahan/CIMA).

stability:
## Stability

- Reconstituted: dilute and use promptly.
- Diluted: ~6 h room temp / ~24 h refrigerated.
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Nausea, diarrhea, headache, rash, phlebitis, ↑ transaminases, positive Coombs, infusion-site reactions.
